To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effect of training leading to failure is not different from the effect of training to volitional exhaustion, and that the effect of failure is different from the effect that occurs when training is performed to volitional exhaustion.

(1) the effect of training leading to repetition failure on muscular strength is small to moderate (d = 0.36), with no evidence of heterogeneity in effect size; (2) the effect of failure training on muscular strength was not influenced by the training volume (d = 2.0), number of training sets (d = 1.8), or training frequency (d = 3.1); (3) the effect of the failure training on muscular endurance is small
the training-induced increase in muscle strength depends on the training intensity (i.e., the load used) and on the training volume (i.e., number of training repetitions).
